plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of blush-white blossoms cover bare branches before the leaves appear. Petals drift down like confetti and carpet parks and riverbanks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April in Washington, D.C., usually peaking around the end of March or the first days of April
plants.funFact: The first Yoshino cherry trees were given to Washington by Tokyo in 1912. Their blossoms last only about a week or two, which is why their timing is closely watched every year.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding golden trumpets surrounded by paler petals appear in woodland clearings and meadows. In good years they cover whole hillsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April in the UK, with many sites in full flower at the end of March
plants.location: Woodlands and meadows of England and Wales, such as the Golden Valley in Herefordshire and the Forest of Dean
plants.funFact: This is the only daffodil native to Britain. It is smaller and more delicate than the garden varieties bred from it.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: Sparkling pink, wavy-petaled flowers rise on slender, leafless stems. They bring bright color to the garden as the southern autumn begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, around March to May, which includes late March
plants.location: Native to the Drakensberg mountains of South Africa, and grown in gardens in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The petals have a faint glittering sheen. This is why nerines are sometimes called Guernsey or jewel lilies.
